original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Decide every rational linear projection/rank cut for a bounded paid-frame multiset before a larger-register scalar search, with exact rejecting witnesses.
scope_change_reason: Live overlap already covers many proposed finite-group identities and the helper-semantic gap. Discussion2200 was stopped by an unautomated rational projection; a complete reusable necessary-condition screen prevents repeating that failed scalar search.
bottleneck_link: A pre-search audit for changed bit-register proposals. It rules out a paid-frame multiset before order/scalar coupling/hosting work; it does not establish a local saving or improve the nonbinding bit supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after the complete paid-span reduction, bounded exact checker, independent small oracle and failure controls. Do not expand into a new candidate census.
evidence: RESULT.json: 16 spans reject the predecessor example with 2 paid versus 3 target labels; direct 9-call word passes; 525 independent integer-functional fixtures agree; 17 invalid-input controls and semantic/receipt mutants pass.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance in derivation, implementation, internal independent checks and writing. No independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can a larger-register candidate pass every rational rank cut and determinant equality, then realize its full formal endpoint?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only a viable full endpoint can justify scalar coupling search and a complete native bill. Passing this screen alone is insufficient.
open_questions.first_step: Save exact candidate JSON and the screen output; for idempotent couplings, check sum paid labels equals sum target labels before scalar search. With nilpotent couplings, first test the corresponding determinant subset-sum condition.
open_questions.blocked_by: No new viable candidate or native caller is constructed in this package.

freshness.compatibility: Guidance, catalogue, selected record, source proof and replay tooling unchanged since scientific base. Current changes are disjoint; retain original exact provenance.

validation.cli_probes: Exit 1 rejection, exit 0 necessary pass, exit 2 invalid type/deep JSON/oversize; integer-to-bool/float receipt mutations reject in subprocesses.
validation.limits: No native/full cold replay, no proof assistant, no hosted CI claim.
